items.title: EU/EEA/Swiss students staying more than 3 months
items.title_it: Studenti UE/SEE/svizzeri che restano più di 3 mesi
items.summary: No residence permit (titre de séjour) is required; a 'carte de séjour étudiant européen' can be requested voluntarily. The right of residence as a student requires enrolment in a recognised institution, sickness-maternity health insurance and sufficient resources (no fixed student amount given). Permanent residence after 5 years of legal continuous residence.
items.notes: Cleiss confirms no student visa is needed for EU/EEA/Swiss nationals whatever the length of stay. UK nationals need a long-stay student visa since 1 January 2021 (Cleiss).

items.title: Non-EU students: long-stay student visa (VLS-TS) and its validation
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: visto lungo soggiorno studente (VLS-TS) e sua convalida

other: Algerian nationals follow a separate regime (certificat de résidence étudiant)

items.summary: The VLS-TS 'étudiant' is valid 4 months to 1 year and must be validated online within 3 months of arrival, paying a €100 tax. Required resources: at least €877.50/month. To stay longer, apply online for a student residence card 4 to 2 months before expiry (€150 = €100 tax + €50 stamp duty; €180 regularisation fee if late). After 1 year, a multi-year card (2–4 years) matching the remaining study cycle can be issued.
steps: Obtain the VLS-TS 'étudiant' from the French consulate before departure
Validate it online within 3 months of arrival and pay the €100 tax
Renew online between 4 and 2 months before expiry (€150)
items.authority: Préfecture / Ministère de l'Intérieur (ANEF online service)
items.notes: The page does not name the ANEF platform explicitly; the online service is the one linked from Service-Public.

items.title: Address registration after arrival
items.summary: None of the official pages consulted (Service-Public F2651, F2231, F13519) mentions an obligation to register with the town hall or a population register. For non-EU students the arrival formality is the online validation of the VLS-TS within 3 months; EU students have no equivalent formality.
items.notes: Absence of a requirement inferred from the pages not mentioning one; no page explicitly states that France has no population register. A human should confirm before the bot says 'no registration needed'.

items.title: Social security number for foreign students
items.title_it: Numero di previdenza sociale (numéro de sécurité sociale) per studenti stranieri

other: EU/EEA/Swiss students only if they register (no valid EHIC, or with an S1 form)

items.summary: Registering on etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr gives a provisional social security number automatically and a provisional attestation; after immatriculation the number is certified, a definitive attestation can be downloaded and a form to request the carte Vitale is sent. Documents: ID/passport, residence permit (non-EU), enrolment certificate, IBAN/RIB, civil-status document.
steps: Keep the provisional number and download the provisional attestation
After validation, download the definitive attestation and request the carte Vitale with the form received
items.notes: No processing times are given on the page. Helpline 09 74 75 36 46 (from abroad +33 974 75 36 46), English-speaking advisers.

items.title: Tax number (numéro fiscal) for foreign students
items.title_it: Numero fiscale (numéro fiscal) per studenti stranieri
items.summary: No official page was found today explaining how a foreign student obtains a French tax number. Students with taxable income should check impots.gouv.fr.

items.title: EU/EEA/Swiss students with a European Health Insurance Card

other: EHIC valid at least until the end of the academic year

items.summary: With an EHIC valid at least until the end of the academic year you stay insured in your home country and do not register on etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr; necessary care is reimbursed as for a French insured person and you pay only the ticket modérateur. Without an EHIC, request one at home; failing that, register on etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr.

items.title: EU/EEA/Swiss students with an S1 form or without EHIC
items.title_it: Studenti UE/SEE/svizzeri con modulo S1 o senza TEAM

other: holds an S1 form, or has neither EHIC nor S1

items.summary: Students with an S1 form (requested at home before leaving) or with no EHIC must register with French health insurance on etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr. Without an S1, a sworn statement of sufficient resources is required. Registration is free.

items.title: EU/EEA/Swiss students who work in France
items.title_it: Studenti UE/SEE/svizzeri che lavorano in Francia

applies_to.min_work_hours: any paid job in France (no threshold stated)

items.summary: EU/EEA and Swiss students who work in France while studying are covered by the French universal health protection (PUMa). The page gives no hour threshold; contact the local CPAM to set up affiliation.

items.title: Non-EU students: free affiliation to French health insurance
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: iscrizione gratuita all'Assurance Maladie

other: Québec students may fall under a bilateral agreement (forms SE 401 Q 106 for exchange, SE 401 Q 102 bis for degree students)

items.summary: Affiliation is mandatory and free for all students in France. Non-EU students register on etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr once they have their enrolment certificate and are covered by PUMa. A complementary insurance (mutuelle) is recommended; low-income students may qualify for the Complémentaire santé solidaire.
items.notes: Service-Public F675 mentions a '3 months uninterrupted residence' condition for PUMa without saying which group it applies to; etudiant.gouv.fr sets no minimum stay for students.

items.title: CVEC student life contribution

other: exchange students who pay no registration fees in France are not concerned

items.summary: Every student in initial higher education must obtain a CVEC certificate (payment or exemption) before enrolling: €105 for 2026-2027. Exempt (but still need the certificate): social-criteria scholarship holders, French government scholarship holders, refugees, subsidiary protection beneficiaries and asylum seekers allowed to stay. Exchange students (e.g. Erasmus+) who pay no registration fees in France are not concerned.
items.notes: Refund requests for 2026-2027 open until 31 May 2027 (cvec.etudiant.gouv.fr).

items.title: Right to a basic bank account (droit au compte)
items.title_it: Diritto a un conto bancario di base (droit au compte)

applies_to.residence_requirement: living in France (any nationality), or legally resident in another EU state; no other deposit account in France

items.summary: If a bank refuses (or does not answer within 15 days), the Banque de France designates a bank within 1 working day that must open a basic account free of charge, with card, transfers, direct debits and cash services. File: ID, proof of address under 3 months, refusal letter, sworn statement of no other account.
steps: Ask a bank to open an account; keep the refusal letter
Submit the file to the Banque de France online, at a branch or by post
Open the account at the designated bank within 6 months
items.cost: Free basic services; overdraft fees capped at €4/operation and €20/month

items.title: Île-de-France: Navigo monthly pass
items.summary: The Navigo Mois pass covering all zones of Île-de-France costs €90.80/month (2026). Employees get at least 50% reimbursed by the employer.
items.notes: Official IDFM and RATP pages refuse automated access; price read on Sciences Po's budget page and matches Numbeo (Nov 2026).

items.title_it: Île-de-France: abbonamento annuale studenti imagine R

other: under 26 on 1 September of the subscription year

€392.30/year, as on Sciences Po's budget page (probably the 2025-2026 price)

items.title: Lyon (TCL): passes for 18-25 and students 26-27
items.title_it: Lione (TCL): abbonamenti 18-25 anni e studenti 26-27 anni
items.summary: From 1 September 2026, the TCL monthly pass for 18-25 year olds and for students aged 26-27 costs €26 (zones 1 and 2, which include Lyon), €35 all zones; annual or 12-month pass €260 (zones 1-2). Scholarship students up to 27 living in TCL zones 1-5 can get the 'solidaire réduit' pass at €11/month.

items.title: Non-EU students: 964 hours per year

other: holds a VLS-TS 'étudiant' or student residence card

items.summary: With a validated VLS-TS or student card you may work up to 964 hours per year (60% of legal annual working time) without separate authorisation, counted from validation/issue. The employer must file a nominal declaration with the préfecture at least 2 working days before hiring. Self-employment (auto-entrepreneur) is not allowed. For a 6-month stay, a work authorisation is needed and hours are pro rata (482 h).
items.notes: Apprenticeship/professionalisation contracts require more than 1 year in France (exception for master's-level apprenticeships). Exceeding 964 h risks withdrawal or non-renewal of the permit.

items.title: Algerian students: work authorisation always required
items.title_it: Studenti algerini: autorizzazione al lavoro sempre necessaria

other: Algerian nationals with a certificat de résidence étudiant

items.summary: The employer must obtain a work authorisation before the student starts; once authorised, the student may work up to 50% of the annual working time of the sector. Self-employment is not allowed.

items.title: European students working in France
items.title_it: Studenti europei che lavorano in Francia
items.summary: No residence permit or work authorisation is needed. Service-Public states that a European student may work up to 964 hours per year (60% of legal annual working time) as a side activity; beyond that the person is treated as a worker rather than a student.

interpretations.hypothesis: 964 h/year is a cap on student work for EU students (page 'Un étudiant européen peut-il travailler en France ?', checked by Service-Public on 18 Nov 2026)
The limit only decides whether the person keeps 'student' status for residence purposes; an EU citizen working more simply resides as a worker, since EU/EEA/Swiss citizens need no titre de séjour

items.title: Statutory minimum wage (SMIC)
items.summary: Adult SMIC: €12.31 gross/hour, €1,867.02 gross/month for 35 h/week (about €9.74 net/hour). Youth rates without 6 months' experience in the sector: €11.08/h at 17, €9.85/h at 16 or under. Apprentices and professionalisation contracts have specific reductions.
items.notes: Amounts per the arrêté of 22 May 2026 (page checked by Service-Public on 1 June 2026); the page does not state the effective date explicitly.
